focus: PlatoTab.tsx state machine and routing — the 6-state body switching logic and the tab container structure

findings.summary: useAiJobApplicationSummary called unconditionally — fires for all 6 states including when no summary exists
findings.spec_requirement: Spec lines 47 and 308: 'Full structured data via useAiJobApplicationSummary — only when a summary exists and status is succeeded' and 'fetch the full data only when status is succeeded and the rich layout needs rendering'
findings.actual_behavior: The hook is called unconditionally at component top level (line 532). When no summary exists, aiSummary?.id is undefined and falls back to 0 (line 534: `aiSummary?.id || 0`), making an API call to `/job_applications/{id}/ai_job_application_summaries/0` which returns a 404. When a summary exists but status is pending/in_progress/extracted/textract_processing/failed, the full structured data is fetched unnecessarily. The underlying useQuery in the hook (useAiJobApplicationSummary.ts line 41) has no `enabled` option, so there is no mechanism to disable the fetch conditionally.
findings.why_it_matters: Every time PlatoTab renders for a candidate without a summary, or with a non-succeeded summary, it fires a wasted API call. For the no-summary case this is a 404 error. The spec explicitly requires lazy fetching to avoid this. Line 537 guards the consumption of the data (`const structuredData = status === 'succeeded' ? ...`) but does not guard the fetch itself.
findings.fix: Add an `enabled` option to the useQuery call in useAiJobApplicationSummary.ts (e.g., `{ enabled: aiJobApplicationSummaryId > 0 }`), or add an `enabled` parameter to the hook interface. Then pass `enabled: summaryExists && status === 'succeeded'` from PlatoTab. Alternatively, since the hook file is not listed in the spec's modified files, it may be acceptable to pass a sentinel and add `enabled: !!aiJobApplicationSummaryId` to the hook — but the hook file must be modified either way.

findings.summary: Route for /ai path not wrapped in FeatureFlipper — accessible when feature flag is off
findings.spec_requirement: Spec line 128: 'Wrap the new route in <FeatureFlipper feature="AI_APPLICANT_SUMMARY">'. Spec line 204: 'When the feature is disabled... the /ai route must redirect to /overview'
findings.actual_behavior: The new <Route path={`${match.path}/ai`}> (diff lines 195-204) is added directly inside the <Switch> block without any FeatureFlipper wrapper. While the possiblePaths array is conditionally gated (diff line 179), that only affects the currentViewPath state for tab highlighting and the redirector fallthrough. The Route itself is matched by React Router's <Switch> before redirector() executes, so a direct URL navigation to /ai when the flag is off will render PlatoTab instead of redirecting to /overview.
findings.why_it_matters: Users with the feature flag disabled can access the Plato tab by navigating directly to the /ai URL. The spec explicitly requires the Route to be wrapped in FeatureFlipper so the route does not match when the flag is off, causing the request to fall through to redirector() which redirects to /overview.
findings.fix: Wrap the <Route> in <FeatureFlipper feature="AI_APPLICANT_SUMMARY">...</FeatureFlipper> as the spec requires. Import FeatureFlipper (the component, not just the hook) if not already imported. The existing import at diff line 161 imports useFeatureFlipper and Features but not the FeatureFlipper component itself — it needs to be added.

verified_correct.requirement: State machine evaluation order: succeeded → pending/in_progress/extracted → textract_processing → failed → no-summary+hasResume → no-summary+no-resume (first match wins)
verified_correct.notes: renderBody() uses if-return chain with summaryExists guards. Order matches spec exactly. Final return renderNoResume() is the correct fallback for row 6.
